instruction: Choose a suitable tool from ANSYS, Abaqus, and AutoCAD to complete the task. On this machine, the available command-line entry points are ANSYS MAPDL at `C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\ansys\bin\winx64\ANSYS261.exe`, Abaqus at `C:\SIMULIA\Commands\abaqus.bat`, and AutoCAD at `C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2024\acad.exe`. Use a command-line or scripting workflow. Use the selected tool to perform a tensile analysis of a thin rectangular shell plate with a central circular hole. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Part: Instantiate a 3D Deformable Shell part. Sketch a rectangle on the XY plane with dimensions 120 mm in the X direction and 240 mm in the Y direction. Cut a circular hole at the center point (60, 120) mm with a diameter of 12 mm. Property: Create a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Homogeneous Shell Section with thickness 1 mm and 5 through-thickness integration points. Assign the section to the entire plate geometry. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the shell plate. Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-HoleTension, placing it after the Initial step. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply shell edge loads of 8 N/mm to the two vertical outer edges. On the left edge at X = 0, apply the load in the global negative X direction. On the right edge at X = 120, apply the load in the global positive X direction. To prevent rigid-body motion without over-constraining the tensile deformation: - At the bottom-left corner (0, 0), constrain U1 = U2 = U3 = 0. - At the bottom-right corner (120, 0), constrain U2 = U3 = 0. - At the top-left corner (0, 240), constrain U3 = 0. Mesh: Seed the circular hole edge with an approximate element size of 2.4 mm. Apply a global seed size of 10 mm to the plate. Assign element type appropriate shell element formulation and generate the mesh. Job: Create a job named Job-FlangeHole, submit it, and wait for successful completion. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and native solver result artifact on the Desktop, and write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/metrics.json` containing exactly three finite numeric fields. Define `max_mises` in MPa as the maximum final-result Mises value over the complete shell mesh and every stored through-thickness shell location: use all integration-point `S.mises` records at every stored section point in Abaqus, or the native per-element `S,EQV` values at the stored TOP and BOTTOM locations and, when stored, MID location in ANSYS. Define the dimensionless `stress_concentration_proxy` as `max_mises / 8.0`. Define `edge_displacement` in mm as the final mean U1 on the right loaded edge minus the final mean U1 on the left loaded edge; a positive value denotes opening. Software launch locations: Abaqus/CAE: `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Abaqus CAE.lnk`; ANSYS: multiple ANSYS launch shortcuts are available under `C:\Users\Public\Desktop`; choose the most suitable ANSYS shortcut for the task; AutoCAD 2024: `C:\Users\Public\Desktop\AutoCAD 2024.lnk`.
